questions.q: What does the column-level lineage UI highlight, compared to the table-level graph?
options: Only the exact upstream columns that fed one specific selected column, not every column in every upstream table
Every column in the entire metastore, regardless of relevance
Only columns that have never been queried
The physical storage size of each column
questions.explain: Column-level lineage narrows the question from 'which tables feed this' to the exact columns that fed one specific column.

questions.q: What does system.access.column_lineage let you do that clicking through the UI diagram once does not?
options: Run a repeatable, exportable SQL query — a real audit tool instead of a one-time visual check
Automatically delete every downstream table that depends on a column
Change a column's data type across every table at once
Nothing — it exposes strictly less information than the UI
questions.explain: The system table exposes the same lineage graph as queryable SQL, turning compliance checks into repeatable, scheduled queries.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what did Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 44 already establish?
options: That lineage is automatic and exists at both table and column level, with zero manual diagram maintenance
The exact SQL syntax for querying system.access.column_lineage
Access control patterns for hundreds of tables at once
File notification mode for Auto Loader
questions.explain: This lesson explicitly recaps that Lesson 44 covered the concept before showing the actual column-level UI and system tables.

questions.q: What real compliance question does column-level lineage make answerable, per this lesson?
options: Which downstream tables contain a column derived from a sensitive source column, such as an SSN
How many total rows exist across the entire metastore
Which cluster size is most cost-effective for a given workload
Which users have logged into the workspace in the last 24 hours
questions.explain: Tracing a sensitive column's downstream footprint is exactly the kind of GDPR/PII audit question column-level lineage answers directly.

questions.q: Why does lineage capture depend on how data was actually processed?
options: Lineage is built by observing real Spark queries against Unity Catalog tables — data loaded by tools bypassing Spark wouldn't appear in the graph
Lineage is manually typed in by an administrator for every table
Lineage only works for tables smaller than a fixed row-count threshold
Lineage capture requires a special separate subscription unrelated to how data is processed
questions.explain: Because capture is observational, only operations that actually ran through Spark against governed tables show up in the graph.
